category: Plasma and Electric Discharge Modules: Interfaces, Chemistry, Boundary Conditions and Studies
description: Physics interfaces, domain/boundary features, chemistry input, multiphysics couplings, study steps and result variables of the COMSOL 6.4 Plasma Module (Plasma, Time Periodic, Drift Diffusion, Heavy Species Transport, Equilibrium Discharges, Charge Transport, Corona Discharge, Electrical Breakdown Detection, Boltzmann equation) and Electric Discharge Module (Electric Discharge, Arc Discharge, Transport of Charge Carriers). Java type strings were verified against the 6.4 Application Library.

tools.name: Plasma, Time Periodic (ptp)
tools.description: Plasma interface specialised for capacitively coupled plasmas (CCP): it solves the periodic steady state of electron, electron-energy, heavy-species and Poisson equations over one RF period directly (the period is an extra dimension), instead of time-stepping thousands of cycles. It shares nodes with Drift Diffusion, Heavy Species Transport and Electrostatics and adds Metal Contact (RF/DC, power or circuit drive), Periodic Excitation, Circuit Options and Surface Charge Accumulation; default nodes are Plasma Model, Zero Charge, Insulation and Initial Values. Studies: Time Periodic and Time Periodic to Time Dependent (1D and 2D axisymmetric per the interface guide).
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Plasma > Plasma, Time Periodic. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("ptp", "ColdPlasmaTimePeriodic", "geom1")

parameters.name: Diffusion model
parameters.description: Mixture-averaged or Fick's law.

parameters.name: Transport settings
parameters.description: Convection, Migration in electric field, thermodynamic properties, full diffusivity, tensor ion transport.

parameters.name: Period / extra-dimension elements
parameters.description: Must match the source frequency; number of elements in the time extra dimension.

parameters.name: Out-of-plane thickness / cross-section
parameters.description: 2D thickness (1 m), 1D axisymmetric height (0.01 m), 1D area (0.01 m^2).

tools.example: Application Libraries Plasma_Module/Capacitively_Coupled_Plasmas/argon_gec_ccp, alpha_to_gamma_transition and ccp_argon_oxygen (13.56 MHz CCP with Metal Contact driven by power).
tools.notes: See 'Capacitively Coupled Plasmas' modelling guidance (1D first, consistent source frequencies and period, extra-dimension resolution). Result averages are available as ptp.neav, ptp.Teav, ptp.Pcap_av.

tools.name: Drift Diffusion (dd)
tools.description: Species-transport interface of the Plasma Module that solves drift–diffusion equations for the electron density and mean electron energy (log formulation), with electron transport properties specified directly, in reduced form, or as tensors for magnetized plasmas. Boundary conditions cover wall losses, secondary and thermionic emission; power can be deposited via General, Inductive or Microwave Power Deposition. Default nodes: Drift–Diffusion Model, Insulation, Initial Values; Time Dependent studies in all dimensions.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Plasma > Species Transport > Drift Diffusion (tag dd)

parameters.name: Use reduced electron transport properties
parameters.description: Input mu_e*N_n etc. (e.g. from the Boltzmann interface).

parameters.name: Compute tensor electron transport properties
parameters.description: For strong DC magnetic fields.

parameters.name: Mean electron energy
parameters.description: Local energy approximation (default), Local field approximation, Fix mean electron energy.

parameters.name: Include thermal diffusion
parameters.description: Adds the gradient-of-diffusivity term.

tools.example: Build a custom discharge: Drift Diffusion (electrons) + Heavy Species Transport (ions/neutrals with Electron Impact Reactions) + Electrostatics, coupled through Electron Production Rate and space charge.
tools.notes: The Plasma interface bundles these three pieces with automatic couplings and is normally preferred. Java type string not present in the 6.4 Application Library.

tools.name: Heavy Species Transport (hs)
tools.description: Species-transport interface of the Plasma Module that adds electron impact reactions, gas-phase reactions, species and surface reactions to plasma models and solves mass fractions of ions and neutrals with Mixture-averaged (default), Fick's law or Global (volume-averaged) diffusion models. Migration in the electric field is on by default; convection, thermodynamic properties, full diffusivity and tensor ion transport are optional. Collision cross sections are most conveniently loaded through Cross Section Import.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Plasma > Species Transport > Heavy Species Transport (tag hs)

parameters.name: Diffusion model
parameters.description: Mixture-averaged, Fick's law or Global.

parameters.name: Transport settings
parameters.description: Migration in electric field (default on), Convection, Calculate thermodynamic properties, Full expression for diffusivity, Compute tensor ion transport properties.

parameters.name: Cross Section Import
parameters.description: File with ELASTIC/EXCITATION/IONIZATION/ATTACHMENT cross sections.

tools.example: Couple to Drift Diffusion by using hs electron-impact source terms as the Electron Production Rate and dd electron properties as model inputs for rate coefficients.
tools.notes: Java type string not present in the 6.4 Application Library. Global diffusion model gives a 0D 'global model' of the reactor.

tools.name: Plasma Model (Plasma domain node)
tools.description: Main domain node of the Plasma and Plasma, Time Periodic interfaces that sets model inputs (gas temperature T, absolute pressure pA, velocity u, DC magnetic flux density B for tensor transport; for Global models the initial temperature, reactor pressure, feed flow and electron flux) and the electron transport properties: Specify mobility only (default, Einstein relation for the rest), From electron impact reactions, From electron energy distribution function, Specify all, Use lookup tables, or Mobility from EEDF (two-term Boltzmann). Reduced (per neutral density) forms are available.
tools.usage: Plasma > Plasma Model 1 (default). Java: physics("plas").feature("pes1") (type PlasmaEsModel); set("T", "300[K]"); set("pA", "1[Torr]"); set("mue", ...)

parameters.name: T, pA, u, B
parameters.description: Model inputs for gas temperature, pressure, velocity and magnetic field.

parameters.name: Electron transport properties
parameters.description: Specify mobility only, From electron impact reactions, From EEDF, Specify all, Use lookup tables, Mobility from EEDF.

parameters.name: mue / muN / De / muen / Den
parameters.description: Electron mobility, diffusivity and energy transport coefficients (or reduced forms).

parameters.name: Global model inputs
parameters.description: Initial temperature, pressure, sccm feed (sccmmfr) and feed temperature.

tools.example: Application Library Plasma_Module/Direct_Current_Discharges/positive_column_1d: argon at 1 Torr, transport properties from electron impact reactions, Wall and Metal Contact boundaries.
tools.notes: The electric field comes from the Poisson equation built into the Plasma interface; Species, reactions and boundary conditions are added as separate nodes.

tools.name: Electron energy distribution function options (Plasma)
tools.description: Plasma interface setting that fixes how rate coefficients are computed from cross-section data: an assumed EEDF (Maxwellian, Druyvesteyn, Generalized with a power-law exponent between 1 and 2, or Function: a 2D interpolation function of electron energy and mean energy, e.g. tabulated with the Boltzmann interface) or a solved Boltzmann equation, two-term approximation (linear or quadratic elements) in an energy extra dimension. The Boltzmann options add Temporal behavior (stationary or time-dependent EEDF), electron–electron collisions, equal secondary energy sharing, oscillating-field correction (reduced angular frequency), energy-grid size (default 100 elements, element ratio 10) and maximum energy (default 100 V or computed).
tools.usage: Plasma > Settings > Electron Energy Distribution Function (requires cross-section-based reactions)

parameters.name: EEDF
parameters.description: Maxwellian, Druyvesteyn, Generalized, Function (interpolated), Boltzmann two-term (linear/quadratic).

parameters.name: Number of elements in EEDF extra dimension N
parameters.description: Default 100.

parameters.name: Maximum energy eps_max / Compute maximum energy
parameters.description: Default 100 V.

parameters.name: Electron–electron collisions, Oscillating field
parameters.description: Advanced Boltzmann options.

tools.example: Application Libraries Plasma_Module/Space-Dependent_EEDF_Modeling/positive_column_1d_boltzmann and argon_gec_icp_boltzmann: EEDF solved in space; initialize with an EEDF Initialization step.
tools.notes: Rate coefficients are available for plotting as <tag>.kf_<n> (e.g. plas.kf_3). Solving the EEDF in space greatly increases model size.

tools.name: Mean electron energy models: Local energy / Local field approximation (Plasma)
tools.description: Choice of how the mean electron energy is obtained in Plasma and Drift Diffusion: Local energy approximation (default) solves the electron energy equation self-consistently and parameterizes transport and rate coefficients by mean energy (most accurate, most nonlinear); Local field approximation assumes coefficients are functions of the reduced field E/N (energy gain balances loss locally), removing the energy equation, with the E/N-to-energy relation from the Boltzmann solver or user input; Fix mean electron energy freezes it at its initial value for quick non-self-consistent models.
tools.usage: Plasma (or Drift Diffusion) > Plasma Properties > Mean electron energy: Local energy approximation | Local field approximation | Fix mean electron energy

parameters.name: Mean electron energy
parameters.description: LEA, LFA or fixed.

parameters.name: Mean Electron Energy Specification (Plasma Model)
parameters.description: Relation between reduced field and energy when LFA is used without the Boltzmann solver.

parameters.name: Reduced electric field plas.Erd
parameters.description: E/N in Td used by LFA.

tools.example: Atmospheric-pressure streamer (Plasma_Module/Direct_Current_Discharges/streamer_1d): LFA with transport data tabulated versus E/N; low-pressure positive column uses LEA.
tools.notes: The Electric Discharge interface also relies on the LFA for atmospheric discharges (p·d > about 200 Torr·cm).

tools.name: Cross Section Import and data file format (Plasma / Boltzmann)
tools.description: Node (and interface-level setting) that loads a set of electron collision cross sections from a text file and automatically creates Electron Impact Reaction features and species. Each block has a keyword line (ELASTIC, EXCITATION, IONIZATION, ATTACHMENT), the reaction formula with =>, a parameter line (mass ratio for elastic; threshold for ionization; energy, statistical-weight ratio and detailed-balance flag for excitation; 0 for attachment), a line of two unit-conversion factors, and a table of energy (eV) versus cross section (m^2) delimited by dashed lines.
tools.usage: Plasma / Heavy Species Transport / Boltzmann Equation, Two-Term Approximation > Cross Section Import > Browse > Import. Java: physics("plas").create("xsec1", "CrossSectionImport", -1); set("Filepath", "Ar_xsecs.txt")

parameters.name: Filepath
parameters.description: Cross-section data file (LXCat-style format described in the Plasma User's Guide).

parameters.name: Detailed balance flag
parameters.description: Third number on EXCITATION lines; 1 creates the reverse (superelastic) reaction.

tools.example:
ELASTIC
e+Ar=>e+Ar
1.36e-5
1.0 1.0
-----
0.0 7.5e-20
...
-----
(Application Library Plasma_Module/Direct_Current_Discharges/argon_dbd_1d imports Ar_xsecs.txt.)
tools.notes: Comment lines may precede each table. Species created automatically still need transport data (Lennard-Jones parameters, mobility) where relevant.

tools.name: Plasma Chemistry Import (Plasma)
tools.description: Node that builds a complete plasma chemistry (species with thermodynamic data, reaction groups of electron-impact and heavy-species reactions, surface reactions and surface reaction groups) from a single text file in the documented format, for Plasma and Plasma, Time Periodic models with tens of species and hundreds of reactions. Imported features are organized automatically into node groups (Species, Surface Species, Surface Reaction).
tools.usage: Plasma > Plasma Chemistry Import > Browse. Java: physics("plas").create("pci1", "PlasmaChemistryImport", -1); set("Filepath", "CF4_O2_plasma_chemistry.txt")

parameters.name: Filepath
parameters.description: Plasma chemistry file (see 'Plasma Chemistry File Format').

tools.example: Application Libraries Plasma_Module/Global_Modeling/cf4_o2_global_model, hydrogen_global_model and sf6_argon_global_model; Plasma_Module/Inductively_Coupled_Plasmas/electrodeless_lamp (Ar/Hg).
tools.notes: Existing species and reactions are regrouped together with imported ones.

tools.name: Electron Impact Reaction (Plasma)
tools.description: Domain feature for a reaction between an electron and a target species (formula such as e+Ar=>2e+Ar+, species created automatically; 'e' is reserved for electrons, ions carry + or - signs). Collision type Elastic, Excitation, Attachment or Ionization with energy loss; the rate is specified from cross-section data with the chosen EEDF, a rate constant (Arrhenius), a Townsend coefficient, or a lookup table. Electron impact reactions are irreversible, but detailed balance in the file creates reverse reactions.
tools.usage: Plasma / Heavy Species Transport / Boltzmann > Electron Impact Reaction. Java: physics("plas").create("eir1", "ElectronImpactReaction", 1); set("formula", "e+Ar=>2e+Ar+"); set("type", "Ionization"); set("de", "15.8")

parameters.name: formula
parameters.description: Reaction formula with =>.

parameters.name: type / de / mratio
parameters.description: Collision type, energy loss (V) and electron/target mass ratio.

parameters.name: SpecifyReactionUsing
parameters.description: UseCrossSectionData, RateConstant, UseLookupTable (Townsend or rate).

parameters.name: eedf
parameters.description: From physics interface property or a local choice (e.g. Maxwellian).

tools.example: Application Library Plasma_Module/Corona_Discharges/corona_discharge_air_1d: ionization, attachment and three-body attachment of a simplified air chemistry specified with Townsend coefficients.
tools.notes: Rate coefficients: plas.kf_<n>; electron source rates feed the electron density and energy equations automatically.

tools.name: Reaction / Reaction Group (Plasma heavy-species chemistry)
tools.description: Reaction defines reversible or irreversible gas-phase reactions not involving electrons (ion–ion recombination, Penning ionization, metastable quenching, three-body reactions) with forward/reverse rate constants or Arrhenius parameters (A, n, E) and optional equilibrium constants; the selection follows the Plasma Model. Reaction Group holds many reactions in one table, as produced by Plasma Chemistry Import, which keeps large mechanisms manageable.
tools.usage: Plasma > Reaction (type Reaction) / Reaction Group (type ReactionGroup). Java: physics("plas").create("rxn1", "Reaction", 1); set("formula", "Ars+Ars=>e+Ar+Ar+"); set("kf", "6.2e-10[cm^3/s]*N_A_const")

parameters.name: formula / rType
parameters.description: Reaction formula; reversible or irreversible.

parameters.name: kf, kr
parameters.description: Forward/reverse rate constants (volumetric units, e.g. m^3/(mol*s)).

parameters.name: useArrhenius, Af, nf, Ef
parameters.description: Arrhenius parameters.

parameters.name: Keq0
parameters.description: Equilibrium constant options.

tools.example: Application Library Plasma_Module/Capacitively_Coupled_Plasmas/alpha_to_gamma_transition: metastable pooling Ars+Ars=>e+Ar+Ar+ and quenching Ars=>Ar.
tools.notes: Rate constants given per molecule (cm^3/s) must be multiplied by N_A_const.

tools.name: Species (Plasma)
tools.description: Species features are created automatically from reaction formulas (or added manually) with species type Neutral, Ion or Electron. Settings include the From mass constraint choice (one neutral species, usually the dominant background gas, is computed from the sum of mass fractions), initial mole/mass fraction or number density, Initial value from electroneutrality for ions, preset species data (molecular weight, Lennard-Jones parameters, thermodynamic polynomials), and mobility specification for ions.
tools.usage: Plasma > Species: <name> (created from formulas; names like Ar_1p for Ar+, O_1m for O-, e for electrons)

parameters.name: From mass constraint
parameters.description: Compute this species from the mass constraint (background gas).

parameters.name: Initial value
parameters.description: Mole fraction, mass fraction or number density; electroneutrality option for ions.

parameters.name: Preset species data / general parameters
parameters.description: M, sigma (Lennard-Jones), epsilon/k, dipole moment, NASA polynomials.

parameters.name: Mobility and diffusivity
parameters.description: Ion mobility specification (e.g. from Lennard-Jones or user defined).

tools.example: Argon discharge: Species Ar (From mass constraint), Ars (metastable, initial fraction 1e-5), Ar_1p (initial value from electroneutrality), e (initial density 1e14 1/m^3).
tools.notes: Names in tables (Species Group, Inflow) must match the species names such as Ar_1p, not Ar+.

tools.name: Surface Reaction / Surface Species (Plasma)
tools.description: Surface Reaction sets irreversible reactions on walls involving gas-phase, surface (Si(s) -> Si_surf) and bulk (Si(b) -> Si_bulk) species, specified by sticking coefficient (with optional Motz–Wise correction and Arrhenius temperature dependence), rate coefficient, sticking coefficient and diffusion (global models), or Bohm velocity for ions. For ion reactants it defines secondary emission coefficient gamma_i (0 to about 0.45) and mean secondary electron energy, and an optional sputter/etch yield. Surface Species are created automatically from surface reactions and add detailed surface chemistry (site coverage, empty site species).
tools.usage: Plasma > Surface Reaction (type SurfaceReaction), Surface Reaction Group (SurfaceReactionGroup); Surface Species appear automatically (SurfaceSpecies). Java: physics("plas").create("sr1", "SurfaceReaction", 0); set("formula", "Ar+=>Ar"); set("gammaf", "0.07")

parameters.name: Specify reaction using
parameters.description: Sticking coefficient, Rate coefficient, Sticking coefficient and diffusion, Bohm velocity.

parameters.name: MotzWise
parameters.description: Motz–Wise correction on/off.

parameters.name: Secondary emission coefficient / mean energy
parameters.description: gamma_i and eps_i for ion impact (e.g. Ar+ on a 5 V work-function surface: 5.8 V).

parameters.name: includeYield, Y0, E_th
parameters.description: Energy-dependent yield (etching/sputtering).

tools.example: Application Libraries Plasma_Module/Surface_Processing/cf4_o2_si_etching_global_model and icp_rf_bias_cf4_o2_si_etching (Si(s), SiF(s), SiF2(s) surface species, ion-enhanced etching yields).
tools.notes: Bulk species are not supported in stationary (including time-periodic) studies.

tools.name: Species Group / Species Constraint Group (Plasma)
tools.description: Convergence and conservation aids for complex plasma chemistries: Species Group lists species containing a common element (first entry a ground-state species in excess) to enforce elemental mass conservation in stationary solutions beyond the single mass constraint, e.g. separate oxygen and nitrogen groups in an Ar/O2/N2 mixture. Species Constraint Group fixes troublesome species at their initial mass fractions so a first study converges, after which a second study (initialized with that solution and the group disabled) lets them evolve.
tools.usage: Plasma > Species Group / Species Constraint Group (type SpeciesConstraintGroup); Species names table

parameters.name: Species names
parameters.description: Exact names as in Species features (e.g. O2, O, O2_1p).

tools.example: Application Library Plasma_Module/Surface_Processing/cf4_o2_si_etching_global_model uses a Species Constraint Group during initialization.
tools.notes: Available in Plasma and Plasma, Time Periodic.

tools.name: Wall (Plasma / Drift Diffusion)
tools.description: Boundary condition for a plasma in contact with a solid: electrons are lost with a thermal flux (reflection coefficient r_e between 0 and 1), optional migration effects (for rapidly varying fields such as DBDs), secondary emission flux and energy flux (taken from Surface Reactions in the Plasma interface), and thermal emission (user defined or Richardson's law with correction factor, work function and surface temperature) with a mean thermionic energy. Density and energy wall conditions can be switched off individually.
tools.usage: Plasma / Drift Diffusion > Wall. Java: physics("plas").create("wall1", "WallDriftDiffusion", 0); set("re", "0.2")

parameters.name: re
parameters.description: Electron reflection coefficient.

parameters.name: incmig
parameters.description: Include migration effects.

parameters.name: ThermalEmissionModel, Phi, T_s, lambda_R
parameters.description: User defined or Richardson's law.

parameters.name: fluxne / fluxen
parameters.description: Use wall condition for electron density / energy.

tools.example: Application Library Plasma_Module/Direct_Current_Discharges/argon_dbd_1d: Wall on both dielectric surfaces with migration effects, plus Surface Charge Accumulation.
tools.notes: Electron Density and Energy (fixed values) should generally be avoided in favour of Wall.

tools.name: Metal Contact (Plasma / Plasma, Time Periodic)
tools.description: Electrode boundary for plasmas. In the Plasma interface it sets a terminal voltage or current with optional circuits (ballast resistor, parallel C with ballast R). In Plasma, Time Periodic it is the powered electrode: Terminal type Voltage, Power (recommended; unique solution) or Circuit, Source RF or RF and DC (with DC bias options), periodic function Cosine, Sine, Pulsed or Dual pulsed, frequency f_p and amplitude or RF power.
tools.usage: Plasma, Time Periodic > Metal Contact. Java: physics("ptp").create("mct1", "MetalContact", 0); set("TerminalType", "PowerTerminal"); set("Prf", "10[W]"); set("fp", "13.56[MHz]")

parameters.name: TerminalType
parameters.description: Voltage, PowerTerminal or Circuit.

parameters.name: Source / PeriodicFunction
parameters.description: RF or RFandDC; Cosine, Sine, Pulsed, Dual Pulsed.

parameters.name: Va / Prf / fp / phase
parameters.description: Voltage amplitude, RF power, frequency and source phase.

parameters.name: CompBias / Vdc / Pdc
parameters.description: DC bias options.

parameters.name: CircuitType (plas)
parameters.description: None, BallastResistor (Rb), ParallelCBallastRCircuit (Cb, Rb).

tools.example: Application Library Plasma_Module/Capacitively_Coupled_Plasmas/pulsed_ccp_discharge (Pulsed periodic function) and Plasma_Module/Direct_Current_Discharges/positive_column_1d (ballast resistor).
tools.notes: The source frequency must be consistent with the interface Period setting. Periodic Excitation subnodes add further frequencies (dual-frequency CCP).

tools.name: Dielectric Contact / Surface Charge Accumulation (Plasma)
tools.description: Boundary conditions where a plasma touches an insulating surface: Dielectric Contact (exterior boundaries adjacent to the Plasma Model) models the wall as a dielectric with surface charge accumulation or a fixed surface charge, optionally with a distributed capacitance (thickness ds, epsilon_r, reference potential) for an unmeshed dielectric layer; Surface Charge Accumulation (interior boundaries between plasma and Charge Conservation domains) solves d(rho_s)/dt = n·J_i + n·J_e so charged species do not leak, with a periodic condition in the time extra dimension for Plasma, Time Periodic.
tools.usage: Plasma > Dielectric Contact (type DielectricContact) / Surface Charge Accumulation (type SurfaceChargeAccumulation)

parameters.name: SurfaceChargeTypeSection
parameters.description: Surface charge accumulation or fixed surface charge density (sigs).

parameters.name: EnableDistributedCapacitance, epsilonrd, ds, Vref
parameters.description: Thin dielectric layer behind the surface.

parameters.name: sigs0
parameters.description: Initial surface charge density.

tools.example: Application Library Plasma_Module/Direct_Current_Discharges/argon_dbd_1d: Surface Charge Accumulation on the dielectric barriers; Plasma_Module/Direct_Current_Discharges/positive_column_2d uses Dielectric Contact on the glass tube.
tools.notes: Always apply Surface Charge Accumulation on plasma/dielectric interior boundaries, otherwise charge leaks from the model.

tools.name: Periodic Excitation / Circuit Options (Plasma, Time Periodic)
tools.description: Periodic Excitation is a subnode of Metal Contact or Terminal that adds another harmonic source (frequency f_p, source phase, voltage amplitude or RF power, cosine/sine) for dual-frequency CCP reactors; its terminal type must match the parent. Circuit Options, used when the terminal type is Circuit, provide a Parallel RC circuit (with optional blocking and stray capacitances), an L–network or a Reversed L–network matching network (match inductance and capacitance) for maximizing power transfer, the L-network suiting plasma resistance below 50 ohm and the reversed one above.
tools.usage: Metal Contact / Terminal > Periodic Excitation; Metal Contact (Terminal type Circuit) > Circuit Options

parameters.name: fp, phase, Va / Prf
parameters.description: Additional source frequency, phase and amplitude/power.

parameters.name: CircuitType
parameters.description: ParallelRCCircuit, LNetwork, Reversed L-network.

parameters.name: Cb, Cs, Lm, Cp
parameters.description: Blocking, stray, match inductance and parallel capacitance.

tools.example: Application Library Plasma_Module/Capacitively_Coupled_Plasmas/impedance_matching: L-network matching of an argon CCP; ccp_benchmark/computing_plasma_impedance compute the plasma impedance first.
tools.notes: All source frequencies must be integer multiples consistent with the period ('Using Consistent Source Frequencies and Period Settings').

tools.name: Capacitive / Inductive Stochastic Heating (Plasma)
tools.description: Domain features that add a stochastic (collisionless) contribution to the electron momentum-transfer collision frequency, applied through a spatial profile and anisotropy vector, to represent nonlocal heating in low-pressure discharges. Capacitive Stochastic Heating offers Collisionless (default), Collisional, Homogeneous or User defined models (plasma bulk thickness, edge-to-center density ratio, sheath voltage amplitude, adjusting coefficient); Inductive Stochastic Heating offers Vahedi (default, low/middle/high alpha regime), Lieberman or User defined (frequency, electron temperature). A Boundary Selection for Stochastic Heating subnode locates the heating region.
tools.usage: Plasma > Capacitive Stochastic Heating / Inductive Stochastic Heating > Boundary Selection for Stochastic Heating

parameters.name: Stochastic frequency model
parameters.description: Collisionless, Collisional, Homogeneous, User defined (capacitive); Vahedi, Lieberman, User defined (inductive).

parameters.name: d, h_l, V, K_s
parameters.description: Bulk thickness, edge-to-center ratio, RF voltage amplitude and adjusting coefficient (capacitive).

parameters.name: f, Te, alpha regime
parameters.description: Inductive source frequency, electron temperature (Local or user defined), regime branch.

tools.example: Low-pressure (1 Pa) argon ICP global model: add Inductive Stochastic Heating (Vahedi, 13.56 MHz) to raise the effective collision frequency and absorbed power.
tools.notes: Java type strings not present in the 6.4 Application Library. For 2D axisymmetric ICPs the Collisionless Heating Coupling offers an effective-viscosity alternative.

tools.name: Drift Diffusion boundary conditions (Electron Density and Energy, Electron Outlet, Flux)
tools.description: Electron boundary conditions of Drift Diffusion and Plasma besides Wall: Electron Density and Energy fixes the electron density (must be nonzero because log(ne) is solved) and/or mean energy on a boundary (to be avoided in favour of Wall); Electron Outlet sets zero normal electron and energy flux at gas outlets; Flux prescribes electron and energy fluxes; Insulation is the default zero-flux condition.
tools.usage: Plasma / Drift Diffusion > Electron Density and Energy (type ElectronDensityAndEnergy) / Electron Outlet (ElectronOutlet) / Flux / Insulation

parameters.name: n_ew
parameters.description: Electron density at the wall (Fix electron density).

parameters.name: Mean electron energy at the wall
parameters.description: Fix mean electron energy (V).

parameters.name: Electron and energy flux
parameters.description: Flux node inputs.

tools.example: Application Libraries Plasma_Module/Direct_Current_Discharges/streamer_2d (Electron Density and Energy) and Plasma_Module/Wave-Heated_Discharges/inplane_microwave_plasma (Electron Outlet at the gas outlet).
tools.notes: Also available as pair conditions where noted in the Drift Diffusion documentation.

tools.name: Drift Diffusion domain sources (Electron Production Rate, General/Inductive/Microwave Power Deposition)
tools.description: Domain features of the Drift Diffusion interface that add sources to the electron equations: Electron Production Rate R_e (1/(m^3·s)) for ionization/attachment rates (typically from Heavy Species Transport); General Power Deposition for an arbitrary electron heat source Q (W/m^3); Inductive Power Deposition (AC/DC Module) for heat from induction currents computed by Magnetic Fields; Microwave Power Deposition (RF Module) for wave heating from Electromagnetic Waves. A Velocity feature adds convection of electrons.
tools.usage: Drift Diffusion > Electron Production Rate / General Power Deposition / Inductive Power Deposition / Microwave Power Deposition / Velocity

parameters.name: R_e
parameters.description: Electron production rate.

parameters.name: Q
parameters.description: Heat source to the electrons (W/m^3), e.g. mf.Qh.

tools.example: Manual ICP model: Magnetic Fields coil at 13.56 MHz, Drift Diffusion with Inductive Power Deposition Q = mf.Qh, Heavy Species Transport providing R_e.
tools.notes: In the Plasma interface these couplings are handled by the Electron Heat Source and Plasma Conductivity Coupling multiphysics nodes.

tools.name: Inflow / Outflow / Heavy Species Flux (Plasma heavy-species boundaries)
tools.description: Heavy-species boundary conditions in Plasma and Heavy Species Transport: Inflow prescribes the inlet composition for gas feeds; Outflow lets species leave by convection; Heavy Species Flux prescribes normal mass fluxes for listed species, by default diffusion plus migration, optionally including convection for injected flows; Symmetry applies zero flux normal to symmetry planes.
tools.usage: Plasma > Inflow (type Inflow) / Outflow (type Outflow) / Heavy Species Flux / Symmetry

parameters.name: Species table
parameters.description: Species names (excluding the From mass constraint species) and values.

parameters.name: Convection (Heavy Species Flux)
parameters.description: Include to prescribe the total flux.

tools.example: Application Library Plasma_Module/Inductively_Coupled_Plasmas/icp_argon_oxygen: Ar/O2 Inflow at the showerhead and Outflow at the pump port with the Nonisothermal Plasma Flow coupling.
tools.notes: Requires Convection to be enabled in the transport settings for Inflow/Outflow to matter.

tools.name: Global Model (Plasma diffusion model Global)
tools.description: Volume-averaged (0D) plasma model selected with Diffusion model = Global in Plasma or Heavy Species Transport: species and electron energy balances without spatial derivatives, with wall losses through h-factors, surface areas and effective diffusion lengths, and a reactor type Closed reactor, Constant mass or Constant pressure (only the latter for stationary studies) with feed and outlet mass flows. Extremely fast, it is ideal for screening complex chemistries and parameter sweeps; an optional heavy species energy equation solves the gas temperature.
tools.usage: Plasma > Settings > Diffusion model: Global; Reactor type; Plasma Model > global model inputs (V, A, feed sccm)

parameters.name: Reactor type
parameters.description: Closed reactor (default), Constant mass, Constant pressure.

parameters.name: Include heavy species energy conservation equation
parameters.description: Solve for the background gas temperature.

parameters.name: hl, LambdaDiff
parameters.description: Surface h-factor and effective diffusion length in Surface Reactions.

parameters.name: sccmmfr, Tfeed
parameters.description: Feed flow and temperature.

tools.example: Application Libraries Plasma_Module/Global_Modeling/chlorine_global_model, cf4_o2_global_model and boltzmann_global_model_argon (global model with a two-term Boltzmann EEDF).
tools.notes: Use Time Dependent studies for closed reactors; stationary only for constant pressure.

tools.name: Inductively Coupled Plasma with RF Bias (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Predefined interface for discharges sustained by induction currents with an additional periodic RF bias on the wafer electrode: Magnetic Fields is solved in the frequency domain and Plasma, Time Periodic solves the periodic steady state, joined by time-periodic versions of Plasma Conductivity Coupling (time-averaged conductivity to mf) and Electron Heat Source (inductive heating, constant over the period). It runs in 2D and 2D axisymmetry with Frequency–Time Periodic and Time Periodic to Time Dependent studies.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Plasma > Inductively Coupled Plasma with RF Bias (adds ptp, mf and couplings). Java: multiphysics().create("pcc1", "PlasmaConductivityTimePeriodicMultiphysicsCoupling", 2); multiphysics().create("ehs1", "ElectronHeatSourceTimePeriodicMultiphysicsCoupling", 2); study FrequencyTimePeriodic

parameters.name: Coil (mf)
parameters.description: ICP coil power or current (AC/DC Module for Coil).

parameters.name: Metal Contact (ptp)
parameters.description: RF bias on the substrate electrode.

parameters.name: Study
parameters.description: Frequency–Time Periodic (type FrequencyTimePeriodic).

tools.example: Application Libraries Plasma_Module/Inductively_Coupled_Plasmas/icp_ccp_argon_chlorine and Plasma_Module/Surface_Processing/icp_rf_bias_cf4_o2_si_etching (ion energy control by wafer bias).
tools.notes: Plain ICP and Microwave Plasma interfaces are catalogued under 'Inductively Coupled Plasma (icp) / Microwave Plasma'. See 'Inductively Coupled Plasma Reactors with RF Bias' for solution strategy.

tools.name: Plasma, Nonisothermal Flow and Nonisothermal Plasma Flow coupling
tools.description: Predefined interfaces (Plasma, Nonisothermal Flow; ICP/Microwave/Time Periodic/ICP with RF Bias, Nonisothermal Flow) that add Laminar Flow and Heat Transfer in Fluids to a plasma model through the Nonisothermal Plasma Flow coupling (nipf1). The coupling passes velocity, pressure and temperature to the Plasma Model, takes thermal conductivity, viscosity, heat capacity and density from the plasma mixture, and returns reaction enthalpy and elastic electron–heavy energy transfer as a heat source.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Plasma > Nonisothermal Plasma Flow > Plasma, Nonisothermal Flow. Java: multiphysics().create("nipf1", "NonIsothermalPlasmaFlowMultiphysicsCoupling", 2)

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Plasma (or ptp), Laminar Flow, Heat Transfer in Fluids.

parameters.name: Density synchronization
parameters.description: Density from the Plasma interface for flow and heat.

tools.example: Application Libraries Plasma_Module/Inductively_Coupled_Plasmas/icp_argon_oxygen and icp_cf4_o2 (gas heating and flow in an ICP etch reactor).
tools.notes: Do not combine with the ordinary Nonisothermal Flow coupling (conflicts). Time-periodic variant type: NonIsothermalPlasmaFlowTimePeriodicMultiphysicsCoupling.

tools.name: Electron Heat Source / Collisionless Heating Coupling (Plasma couplings)
tools.description: Plasma multiphysics couplings for wave- or induction-heated discharges: Electron Heat Source (ehs1) applies the heat source from Magnetic Fields or Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain to the electron energy equation of Plasma or Plasma, Time Periodic (constant over the period in the latter); Collisionless Heating Coupling (2D axisymmetric only) adds nonlocal heating effects through an effective viscosity approximation, important below about 2 Pa and above about 10 MHz.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Electron Heat Source (type ElectronHeatSourceMultiphysicsCoupling) / Collisionless Heating Coupling

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Plasma (or ptp) and mf or ewfd (locked selection = intersection).

tools.example: Application Library Plasma_Module/Inductively_Coupled_Plasmas/argon_gec_icp: Electron Heat Source + Plasma Conductivity Coupling between mf and plas, Frequency–Transient study.
tools.notes: Collisionless Heating Coupling Java type not present in the 6.4 Application Library.

tools.name: Equilibrium Discharges (multiphysics interfaces)
tools.description: Predefined interfaces for thermal (LTE) plasmas such as arcs and ICP torches: Equilibrium Discharges (3D) and Equilibrium Discharges, In-Plane Currents (2D/2D axisymmetric) couple Magnetic and Electric Fields, Heat Transfer in Fluids and Laminar Flow with Magnetohydrodynamics and Equilibrium Discharge Heat Source; Equilibrium Discharges, Out-of-Plane Currents uses the cheaper Magnetic Fields interface (no current conservation, no electrode ion/electron heating). Studies: Stationary, Time Dependent, Frequency–Stationary and Frequency–Transient.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Plasma > Equilibrium Discharges > Equilibrium Discharges / In-Plane Currents / Out-of-Plane Currents

parameters.name: Constituent interfaces
parameters.description: mef (or mf), ht (fluids), spf.

parameters.name: Couplings
parameters.description: Magnetohydrodynamics, Equilibrium Discharge Heat Source, Equilibrium Discharge Boundary Heat Source.

parameters.name: Plasma material
parameters.description: Temperature-dependent conductivity, enthalpy, radiation (net emission coefficient) of the gas.

tools.example: Application Libraries Plasma_Module/Equilibrium_Discharges/plasma_dc_arc, plasma_pulsed_arc and icp_torch.
tools.notes: Requires AC/DC Module; the obsolete Static/Induction Current Density Component and Lorentz Force couplings are replaced by mef and Magnetohydrodynamics.

tools.name: Equilibrium Discharge Heat Source / Boundary Heat Source (couplings)
tools.description: Couplings of the equilibrium discharge and arc interfaces: Equilibrium Discharge Heat Source (phs1) puts Joule heating, volumetric net radiation loss (total volumetric emission coefficient from material) and enthalpy transport by the current into the heat equation, each switchable; Equilibrium Discharge Boundary Heat Source (bphs1) maps electrode surface heating for Anode (work function, default 4.15 V) or Cathode (thermionic electron current with effective Richardson constant 120 A/(m^2·K^2) and effective work function 2.6 V, ion current with ionization potential 15.7 V).
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Equilibrium Discharge Heat Source (type EquilibriumDischargeHeatSource) / Equilibrium Discharge Boundary Heat Source (type EquilibriumDischargeBoundaryHeatSource)

parameters.name: Include enthalpy transport / Joule heating / volumetric net radiation loss
parameters.description: Heat source components (all on by default).

parameters.name: Q_rad
parameters.description: Total volumetric emission coefficient (From material or user defined).

parameters.name: Electrode polarity, Phi, A_R*, Phi_eff, V_ion
parameters.description: Boundary heat source electrode data.

tools.example: Application Library Electric_Discharge_Module/Arc_Discharges/free_burning_argon_arc and Plasma_Module/Equilibrium_Discharges/plasma_dc_arc (anode and cathode boundary heat sources).
tools.notes: Used by both the Plasma Module (Equilibrium Discharges) and Electric Discharge Module (Arc Discharge).

tools.name: Charge Transport (ct)
tools.description: Plasma Module interface that solves for the space charge density of one carrier polarity (positive or negative ions) transported by migration in the electric field and optionally convection, stationary in all dimensions. It is the transport half of the Corona Discharge interface; default nodes Transport Properties (charge number, reduced ion mobility, T, p), No Flux and Initial Values, plus Source (current source or reaction rate) and Space Charge Density (fixed rho or number density) boundaries.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Plasma > Species Transport > Charge Transport. Java: physics().create("ct", "ChargeTransport", "geom1")

parameters.name: Convection
parameters.description: Add flow convection to migration.

parameters.name: zq, muiN, T, pA
parameters.description: Charge number, reduced mobility, temperature and pressure (Transport Properties).

parameters.name: Source
parameters.description: Current source S (A/m^3) or reaction rate R.

parameters.name: Space Charge Density BC
parameters.description: rho0 or number density n0.

tools.example: Application Library Plasma_Module/Corona_Discharges/electrostatic_precipitator: ct + es coupled for the ion space charge, EHD force ct.Fehdx/ct.Fehdy passed to the gas flow and particle tracing.
tools.notes: Stationary study only.

tools.name: Corona Discharge (multiphysics interface with Electrode, Space Charge Density and Potential Couplings)
tools.description: Predefined stationary interface for the drift region of unipolar corona discharges: Electrostatics + Charge Transport joined by Space Charge Density Coupling (ion space charge into Poisson's equation) and Potential Coupling (potential into the ion migration term). The ionization layer is not resolved; the Electrode multiphysics node on the corona wire sets the potential V0 and the surface electric field E0 from Peek's law (disruptive field Ec, empirical constant c, electrode radius rc) or a user value, finding the emitted charge density with a Lagrange multiplier.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Plasma > Corona Discharge (adds es, ct, scdc1, pc1); Multiphysics > Electrode (add manually). Java: multiphysics().create("el1", "Electrode", 1)

parameters.name: Electrode: V0
parameters.description: Corona electrode potential.

parameters.name: Electrode electric field
parameters.description: Peek's law (Ec, c, rc) or User defined E0.

parameters.name: Charge Transport polarity
parameters.description: Positive or negative ions.

tools.example: Application Library Plasma_Module/Corona_Discharges/positive_and_negative_corona_discharges: current–voltage characteristics for both polarities from a wire in a cylinder.
tools.notes: Stationary only; the Electric Discharge interface resolves the ionization region in time-dependent simulations.

tools.name: Electrical Breakdown Detection (ebd)
tools.description: Particle-based interface (Plasma and Electric Discharge Modules) that estimates whether electrical breakdown occurs between excited and grounded surfaces: test particles are released from Cathode boundaries along electric field lines (field from an Electrostatics or Electric Currents study) and the Townsend growth coefficient is integrated along each path and compared with the threshold ln(1 + 1/gamma_i). The domain node sets gas number density (pressure and temperature) and the Townsend coefficient from built-in Dry air data, a lookup table versus reduced field, or A·exp(-B/(E/p))-type coefficients.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Plasma > Electrical Breakdown Detection. Java: physics().create("ebd", "ElectricalBreakdownDetection", "geom1"); physics("ebd").create("cod1", "Cathode", 2)

parameters.name: NumberDensitySpecification, pA, T, Nd
parameters.description: Pressure and temperature (ideal gas) or number density.

parameters.name: SpecifyTownsendCoefficientUsing
parameters.description: DryAir, Lookup table (E/N in Td vs alpha/N), or Coefficients (At, Bt).

parameters.name: SpecifyElectricFieldUsing
parameters.description: Electric field from another interface or expression.

parameters.name: Additional variables
parameters.description: Store trajectory information for postprocessing.

tools.example: Application Libraries Plasma_Module/Electrical_Breakdown_Detection/breakdown_between_spheres and Electric_Discharge_Module/Streamer_Discharges/breakdown_between_spheres (electric field from an Electrostatics study, then test-particle release from the cathode sphere).
tools.notes: Default nodes: Electrical Breakdown Detection and Wall; at least one Cathode is required.

tools.name: Cathode / Particle Counter / Nonlocal Accumulator (Electrical Breakdown Detection)
tools.description: Features of Electrical Breakdown Detection: Cathode releases test particles (one per surface mesh element times the Refinement factor) and holds the secondary emission coefficient gamma_i (default 0.07, typically 0.001–0.4) and a minimum field for sustained propagation; Nonlocal Accumulator (Cathode subnode) transfers a quantity accumulated along a particle path back to its release point (Density or Count, over elements or elements and time); Particle Counter reports numbers and transmission probability of particles reaching selected domains/boundaries.
tools.usage: Electrical Breakdown Detection > Cathode (type Cathode) > Nonlocal Accumulator; Particle Counter (type ParticleCounter)

parameters.name: gammai
parameters.description: Secondary emission coefficient.

parameters.name: Emin
parameters.description: Minimum field for sustained propagation.

parameters.name: RefinementFactor
parameters.description: Particles released per boundary element.

parameters.name: Accumulated variable name / Source R
parameters.description: Nonlocal Accumulator definition (default name rpi).

tools.example: Application Library Plasma_Module/Electrical_Breakdown_Detection/breakdown_between_spheres: Cathode gammai = 0.07, Emin = 4.7 kV/cm, Particle Counter on the anode sphere.
tools.notes: Plot the breakdown indicator on the cathode surface using the nonlocal accumulator variable.

tools.name: Boltzmann Model (Boltzmann Equation, Two-Term Approximation)
tools.description: Global node of the 0D Boltzmann Equation, Two-Term Approximation interface where the discharge parameters are set: gas temperature Tg (default 300 K), absolute pressure pA (1 atm; used for time-dependent EEDF), electron density and ionization degree when electron–electron collisions are active, the reduced electric field E/N or mean energy, gas composition (mole fractions of target species), and which derived quantities to plot (transport properties, rate and Townsend coefficients, collision frequencies, energy losses, cross sections).
tools.usage: Boltzmann Equation, Two-Term Approximation > Boltzmann Model. Java: physics("be").feature("bmdl1") (type BoltzmannModel); set("Tg", "300[K]"); set("Erd", "100[Td]")

parameters.name: Tg, pA
parameters.description: Gas temperature and pressure.

parameters.name: Erd
parameters.description: Reduced electric field (Td), may be time dependent.

parameters.name: x / Species
parameters.description: Mole fractions of the collision targets.

parameters.name: ne, beta
parameters.description: Electron density and ionization degree (electron–electron collisions).

parameters.name: TransportPropPG, TownCoefPG, RateCoefPG...
parameters.description: Default plot group generation flags.

tools.example: Application Libraries Plasma_Module/Two-Term_Boltzmann_Equation/boltzmann_dry_air and transient_negative_mobility (time-dependent E/N pulses).
tools.notes: Results: be.f (EEDF), be.ebar (mean energy), be.muN, be.DeN, rate coefficients be.k_<n>, Townsend coefficients be.alpha_<n>.

tools.name: Time Periodic / Time Periodic to Time Dependent / Frequency–Time Periodic (plasma study steps)
tools.description: Study steps for periodic plasma solutions: Time Periodic (Plasma, Time Periodic) behaves like a Stationary step and computes the periodic steady state over one RF period; Time Periodic to Time Dependent converts a periodic solution into an ordinary time-dependent one (e.g. to continue with pulses or extract waveforms); Frequency–Time Periodic (ICP with RF Bias) solves the frequency-domain magnetic field together with the time-periodic plasma. Settings follow the Stationary and Time Dependent steps.
tools.usage: Add Study > Time Periodic / Time Periodic to Time Dependent / Frequency–Time Periodic. Java: model.study("std1").create("tper", "TimePeriodic"); create("tptd", "TimePeriodicToTimeDependent"); create("ftper", "FrequencyTimePeriodic")

parameters.name: Period
parameters.description: Defined in the ptp interface; must match source frequencies.

parameters.name: Parametric sweeps
parameters.description: Power or pressure sweeps with previous-solution continuation.

tools.example: Application Library Plasma_Module/Capacitively_Coupled_Plasmas/argon_gec_ccp: Time Periodic study with an auxiliary sweep over input power, followed by Time Periodic to Time Dependent for waveform plots.
tools.notes: Converge at low power first; mesh the extra time dimension sufficiently ('Choosing the Number of Elements in the Extra Dimension').

tools.name: EEDF Initialization / Mean Energies / Reduced Electric Fields (Boltzmann study steps)
tools.description: Study steps tied to the electron energy distribution: EEDF Initialization (Plasma, Plasma Time Periodic, ICP and Microwave Plasma) initializes the EEDF when it is computed with the two-term Boltzmann approximation, before the main step; Mean Energies and Reduced Electric Fields (Boltzmann Equation, Two-Term Approximation) sweep lists of mean electron energies or E/N values to tabulate transport properties, rate and Townsend coefficients for use in fluid plasma models. Values can be typed with range() or loaded from a file.
tools.usage: Add Study > EEDF Initialization / Mean Energies / Reduced Electric Fields. Java: model.study("std1").create("edfi", "EEDFInitialization"); create("ebar", "MeanEnergies"); create("ref", "ReducedElectricFields")

parameters.name: Mean energies
parameters.description: List of mean electron energies (V).

parameters.name: Reduced electric fields
parameters.description: List of E/N values (Td).

parameters.name: Load parameter values
parameters.description: Read the list from a file.

tools.example: Application Library Plasma_Module/Two-Term_Boltzmann_Equation/boltzmann_argon: Reduced Electric Fields sweep 1–1000 Td, export of mobility and ionization rate tables; Plasma_Module/Global_Modeling/boltzmann_global_model_argon uses EEDF Initialization.
tools.notes: Tabulated data can be loaded into Plasma Model 'Use lookup tables' or Electron Impact Reaction lookup tables.

tools.name: Plasma result variables (plas.ne, plas.Te, plas.Erd, plas.kf_<n>, ptp.neav, ptp.Pcap_av)
tools.description: Key postprocessing variables of the plasma interfaces: electron density plas.ne, electron temperature plas.Te, neutral density plas.Nn, reduced field plas.Erd, rate coefficients plas.kf_<n>, space charge plas.scharge, species number densities such as plas.n_wAr_1p, electron velocity components plas.vnex; for Plasma, Time Periodic the period averages ptp.neav, ptp.Teav, ptp.Pcap_av (absorbed power), ptp.Pcap_ions_av and ptp.Vav, plus time-extra-dimension values; for the Boltzmann interface be.f, be.ebar, be.muN, be.k_<n>, be.alpha_<n>.
tools.usage: Results > Line Graph of plas.ne and plas.Te; Global Evaluation of ptp.Pcap_av; 1D plot of be.f versus energy

parameters.name: plas.ne / plas.Te
parameters.description: Electron density (1/m^3) and temperature (V).

parameters.name: ptp.<var>av
parameters.description: Period-averaged quantities in Plasma, Time Periodic.

parameters.name: n_w<species>
parameters.description: Species number density.

tools.example: Plot the axial ion density: Line Graph expression plas.n_wAr_1p on the discharge axis; check power balance with ptp.Pcap_av versus the requested RF power.
tools.notes: Names confirmed from expressions in the 6.4 Plasma Module Application Library.

tools.name: Electric Discharge (edis)
tools.description: Electric Discharge Module interface for discharges and breakdown in gas, liquid and solid dielectrics: built-in charge transport models solve drift–diffusion equations of electrons, holes, positive and negative ions fully coupled with Poisson's equation, plus surface charge accumulation and relaxation at dielectric interfaces. Typical uses are streamers, corona and Trichel pulses, DBDs and surface DBDs, ESD, partial discharges and liquid/solid dielectric breakdown; it supports 1D–3D and axisymmetric components with Time Dependent, Stationary and Frequency-Domain Perturbation studies.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Electric Discharge > Electric Discharge. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("edis", "ElectricDischarge", "geom1")

parameters.name: Dielectric medium selection
parameters.description: Gas (default), Liquid, Solid checkboxes (adds the corresponding domain nodes).

parameters.name: Out-of-plane thickness / cross-sectional area
parameters.description: Default 1 cm / 1 cm^2, used for terminal currents.

parameters.name: Consistent stabilization
parameters.description: Streamline diffusion (default on) and isotropic diffusion.

parameters.name: Result variables
parameters.description: edis.n_e, edis.logn_e, edis.rhos, edis.I0_<n>, Joule heating power Q_j and EHD force (edis.Fx, edis.Fy, edis.Fz) for coupling to heat transfer and flow, edis.minDRT (minimum dielectric relaxation time).

tools.example: Application Libraries Electric_Discharge_Module/Corona_Discharges/corona_discharge_iv_curve, trichel_pulses and Electric_Discharge_Module/Dielectric_Barrier_Discharges/dbd.
tools.notes: Fluid approximation valid for p·d > 0.1 Torr·cm and E/N up to 1500 Td; the interface focuses on the local field approximation regime (p·d > 200 Torr·cm). Use the Plasma interface for low-pressure plasmas. Start with an Electrostatics Initialization step.

tools.name: Gas (Electric Discharge)
tools.description: Domain node for gaseous dielectrics in the Electric Discharge interface. Material model Insulator (Poisson only, like Charge Conservation), Conductor (like Current Conservation) or Charge transport with carriers Electrons, positive and negative ions / Electrons and positive ions / Positive and negative ions. Charge transport options: background ionization (default about 10 pairs/(cm^3·s)), transport mechanisms (electric-field drift always, magnetic-field drift, convection, diffusion via Einstein relation or user values), and reaction coefficients for impact ionization, attachment and recombination From material (Electric Discharge material library) or user defined; temperature and pressure are model inputs.
tools.usage: Electric Discharge > Gas. Java: physics("edis").feature("gas1"); set("MaterialModel", "ChargeTransport"); set("ChargeCarriers", "e_p_n")

parameters.name: MaterialModel / ChargeCarriers
parameters.description: Insulator, Conductor or ChargeTransport; e_p_n, e_p, p_n.

parameters.name: includeRB / RB
parameters.description: Background ionization rate (default 10 1/(cm^3·s)).

parameters.name: MigrationM, Convection, Diffusion
parameters.description: Magnetic drift, flow convection, diffusion switches.

parameters.name: mu_e, mu_p, mu_n, alpha, eta, beta_ep, beta_pn
parameters.description: Mobilities, ionization and attachment coefficients, recombination coefficients.

tools.example: Application Library Electric_Discharge_Module/Streamer_Discharges/double_headed_streamer: air with electrons and positive ions, Photoionization subnode, Time Dependent study in 2D axisymmetry.
tools.notes: Add Photoionization for positive streamers. Dielectric model: Relative permittivity or Polarization.

tools.name: Liquid (Electric Discharge)
tools.description: Domain node for liquid dielectrics such as transformer oil: Insulator, Conductor or Charge transport with Electrons, positive and negative ions / Electrons and positive ions / Positive and negative ions, background ionization (on by default), drift, convection and diffusion switches, and liquid-specific field ionization parameters (molecular number density, molecular separation a, effective mass, ionization potential) in addition to recombination. A Dissociation subnode adds field-enhanced dissociation (Wien/Onsager effect).
tools.usage: Electric Discharge (Liquid checked) > Liquid. Java: physics("edis").feature("liquid1"); set("ChargeCarriers", "p_n")

parameters.name: MaterialModel / ChargeCarriers
parameters.description: ChargeTransport with e_p_n, e_p or p_n.

parameters.name: n_ioni, a, m_eff, phi_Delta
parameters.description: Field-ionization (Zener-type) parameters of the liquid.

parameters.name: Convection
parameters.description: Couple to Laminar Flow velocity for EHD flows.

tools.example: Application Libraries Electric_Discharge_Module/Liquid_Dielectrics/streamer_in_transformer_oil and ehd_flow_dielectric_liquid.
tools.notes: Time step control with edis.minDRT is recommended for highly conducting liquids.

tools.name: Solid (Electric Discharge)
tools.description: Domain node for solid dielectrics (insulators, polymers, poor conductors): Insulator, Conductor or Charge transport with the bipolar model Electrons and holes, mobile and trapped, including hopping mobilities, trapping/detrapping with trap depths and attempt frequencies, recombination and background ionization. It captures space-charge accumulation in HVDC cable insulation and charge injection from electrodes (via Electrode surface emission).
tools.usage: Electric Discharge (Solid checked) > Solid. Java: physics("edis").feature("solid1"); set("MaterialModel", "ChargeTransport"); set("ChargeCarriers", "e_h_te_th")

parameters.name: ChargeCarriers
parameters.description: e_h_te_th (electrons and holes, mobile and trapped).

parameters.name: mu_be, mu_bh, phi_st_e, phi_st_h
parameters.description: Effective mobilities and shallow trap depths.

parameters.name: nu_te, nu_th, phi_te, phi_th
parameters.description: Detrapping attempt frequencies and deep trap depths.

parameters.name: epsilonr
parameters.description: Relative permittivity.

tools.example: Application Library Electric_Discharge_Module/Solid_Dielectrics/charge_transport_in_polyethylene: space charge build-up in LDPE under DC stress with Schottky injection.
tools.notes: Theory: 'Bipolar Charge Transport in Solids' in the Electric Discharge User's Guide.

tools.name: Electrode / Floating Electrode (Electric Discharge)
tools.description: Boundary subfeatures for metal surfaces (the metal domain itself is excluded from the model). Electrode sets a terminal (Voltage or Circuit) and carrier boundary conditions: No diffusive flux (default), Number density, Open boundary, No flux, Flux or Surface emission, where emission can be secondary electron emission and field electron emission (gas), thermionic emission with optional Schottky lowering (all media). Floating Electrode models an isolated metal with equal potential: prescribed total charge (insulator), current (conductor) or charge integrated from the discharge current (charge transport) with an initial surface charge.
tools.usage: Electric Discharge > Gas/Liquid/Solid > Electrode (type Electrode) / Floating Electrode (type FloatingElectrode). Java: feature("gas1").create("ece1", "Electrode", 1); set("TerminalType", "Voltage"); set("V0", "V0*rm1(t/10[us])")

parameters.name: TerminalName / TerminalType / V0
parameters.description: Terminal definition (Voltage or CircuitVoltage).

parameters.name: eBnd, pBnd, nBnd, hBnd
parameters.description: Boundary condition per carrier (NoDiffusiveFlux, NumberDensity, SurfaceEmission...).

parameters.name: SecondaryElectronEmission / FieldElectronEmission / ThermionicEmission / SchottkyEffect
parameters.description: Emission mechanisms (secondary emission gamma, Fermi energy, work function phi and injection barriers).

parameters.name: Q0, I0 (Floating Electrode)
parameters.description: Total charge or current.

tools.example: Application Libraries Electric_Discharge_Module/Corona_Discharges/trichel_pulses (secondary emission at the cathode) and Electric_Discharge_Module/Streamer_Discharges/streamer_from_metal_particles (Floating Electrode).
tools.notes: Circuit terminals connect to the Electrical Circuit interface (e.g. Electric_Discharge_Module/Electrostatic_Discharges/esd).

tools.name: Dielectric Interface, Bulk / Surface Transport (Electric Discharge)
tools.description: Default features at boundaries between different dielectric media (gas–solid, gas–liquid, liquid–solid): Dielectric Interface, Bulk Transport (subfeature) sets carrier boundary conditions (no diffusive flux, number density, surface emission...) on each side, and Dielectric Interface, Surface Transport (available when more than one medium is selected) solves surface charge accumulation and relaxation, optionally with surface conduction (surface conductivity sigma_s) and an initial surface charge.
tools.usage: Electric Discharge > Dielectric Interface, Surface Transport (type DielectricInterfaceSurfaceTransport) and its Bulk Transport subnodes (type DielectricInterfaceBulkTransport)

parameters.name: MaterialInterface
parameters.description: Automatic detection of adjacent media.

parameters.name: rhos0 / SurfaceChargeDensity
parameters.description: Initial or fixed surface charge.

parameters.name: SurfaceConduction / sigmas
parameters.description: Enable surface conduction and set the surface conductivity sigma_s.

parameters.name: eBnd, pBnd ... emission options
parameters.description: Per-carrier bulk boundary conditions.

tools.example: Application Libraries Electric_Discharge_Module/Dielectric_Barrier_Discharges/sdbd and negative_surface_discharge: surface charge build-up on the barrier during a surface DBD.
tools.notes: Theory: 'Charge Transport at Dielectric Interfaces'.

tools.name: Photoionization / Dissociation (Electric Discharge subnodes)
tools.description: Source subnodes: Photoionization (under Gas, when electrons and positive ions are solved) models nonlocal photoionization essential for positive streamers with an N_fit-term exponential-fit approximation (default 3 terms, linear elements, air parameters: quenching pressure, efficiency xi, A_j and lambda_j coefficients); Dissociation (under Liquid, with positive and negative ions) adds field-enhanced molecular dissociation (Wien/Onsager effect) using the zero-field conductivity, with ion–ion recombination handled by the parent.
tools.usage: Gas > Photoionization (type Photoionization); Liquid > Dissociation (type Dissociation). Java: feature("gas1").create("pi1", "Photoionization", 2); set("N_fit", "3")

parameters.name: N_fit, order
parameters.description: Number of exponential terms and element order.

parameters.name: p_p, p_q, xi
parameters.description: Pressure, quenching pressure (30 Torr in air) and photoionization efficiency.

parameters.name: A_j, lambda_j
parameters.description: Fit coefficients per term.

parameters.name: sigma_0 (Dissociation)
parameters.description: Zero-field conductivity (From material or user defined).

tools.example: Application Libraries Electric_Discharge_Module/Corona_Discharges/positive_glow_corona and Electric_Discharge_Module/Streamer_Discharges/streamer_in_weak_field (Photoionization); Electric_Discharge_Module/Liquid_Dielectrics/ehd_flow_dielectric_liquid (Dissociation).
tools.notes: Photoionization adds extra dependent variables per exponential term.

tools.name: Arc Discharge (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Electric Discharge Module interface for fully ionized arc discharges in an MHD framework: Magnetic and Electric Fields, Heat Transfer in Fluids and Laminar Flow joined by Magnetohydrodynamics and Equilibrium Discharge Heat Source couplings (Joule heating, enthalpy transport by current, radiation loss), with optional boundary heat sources at electrodes. Supports Time Dependent, Stationary, Frequency–Transient and Frequency–Stationary studies for circuit breakers, arc welding and plasma torches.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Electric Discharge > Arc Discharge (adds mef, ht, spf, mhd1, phs1). Java: multiphysics().create("phs1", "EquilibriumDischargeHeatSource", 2); multiphysics().create("mhd1", "Magnetohydrodynamics", 2)

parameters.name: Plasma gas material
parameters.description: Temperature-dependent LTE properties (conductivity, enthalpy, viscosity, net emission coefficient).

parameters.name: Couplings

tools.name: Transport of Charge Carriers (tcc)
tools.description: General interface (Electric Discharge and Semiconductor Modules) for number densities of one or more charge carriers or neutral species transported by electric-field drift (coupled to an electromagnetic interface), magnetic-field drift, convection and diffusion, with reactions. Nodes: Transport Properties (E, B, velocity sources; mobility and diffusion tensors; carrier charge numbers), Reactions, Number Density, Open Boundary, No Flux, Flux, No Diffusive Flux, Symmetry, Periodic Condition and Current Calculation (terminal current through a boundary).
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Electric Discharge > Transport of Charge Carriers. Java: physics().create("tcc", "TransportOfChargeCarriers", "geom1"); physics("tcc").create("ccal1", "CurrentCalculation", 1)

parameters.name: Transport mechanisms
parameters.description: Electric field drift, Magnetic field drift, Convection, Diffusion.

parameters.name: mu, D, z_<species>
parameters.description: Mobility and diffusivity tensors and charge numbers (Transport Properties).

parameters.name: Reactions R_n
parameters.description: Rate expressions per species.

parameters.name: Current Calculation terminal name
parameters.description: Integrates carrier current over a boundary.

tools.example: Application Libraries Electric_Discharge_Module/Streamer_Discharges/double_headed_streamer_discharge_chemistry (tcc + Chemistry), Semiconductor_Module/Device_Building_Blocks/memristor and Semiconductor_Module/Transistors/egofet (ionic transport with Current Calculation).
tools.notes: Stationary, Time Dependent and Frequency-Domain Perturbation studies; log formulation variables tcc.logn_<species>.

tools.name: Electrostatics Initialization (Electric Discharge study step)
tools.description: Study step that solves only the electrostatic equations of the model, neglecting charge transport in the Electric Discharge interface, to provide consistent initial values when an electric field is present at time zero. It is the standard first step before the Time Dependent step in Electric Discharge Module models.
tools.usage: Add Study > Electrostatics Initialization (preset 'Time Dependent with Initialization' style sequence). Java: model.study("std1").create("esi", "ElectrostaticsInitialization")

parameters.name: Physics selection
parameters.description: Solves the Poisson part only; carrier densities keep initial values.

parameters.name: Follow-up step
parameters.description: Time Dependent using this solution as initial values.

tools.example: Application Library Electric_Discharge_Module/Corona_Discharges/corona_discharge_iv_curve: Electrostatics Initialization followed by a Time Dependent step and a parametric voltage sweep.
tools.notes: Available with the Electric Discharge interface.
